paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Jesus was dead and buried, and a stone was rolled against the entrance of the tomb (Mark 15:46). The women walked to that tomb to anoint a body, and they were worried about a stone (Mark 16:1-3). But the stone was already rolled away, and the young man in the white robe told them, "He has risen! He is not here!" (Mark 16:6).

So the lesson is this: the resurrection is the center of everything, and it doesn't depend on us being ready for it. The women came with spices, expecting a tomb that was closed. God had already done what they couldn't. I think that's good news for every baker who has ever stood in front of a problem that looked WAY too big, because the stone was never theirs to move.

Then look at what the young man says next. He sends the women to the disciples and Peter with this message: "He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you" (Mark 16:7). Jesus keeps His word, and He goes ahead of His people. The women ran away trembling and said nothing in their fear (Mark 16:8), and that tells me you can be scared and still be standing on solid ground. The story isn't over, friend, so keep your apron on.
